lookupPage.activeOnesFromEveryFeed: The active ones, from every feed.
lookupPage.n198511007Bad: 198.51.100.7, bad.example.com, a URL or a hash
lookupPage.noActiveIndicatorMatchesThat: No active indicator matches. That says nothing good about it, only that no feed has it.
lookupPage.isItKnownToBeBad: Is an address, domain, URL, email address or file hash known to be bad? Defanged values such as hxxp://bad[.]example are read too.

indicatorDialog.intoAManualFeedWhat: Into a manual feed. What you leave empty takes the feed's defaults.
indicatorDialog.anAdminAddsAFeed: An admin adds a feed of kind Manual under

indicatorsPage.whatTheFeedsSayIs: What the feeds say is bad, for how long, and how sure they are. TLP:RED is shown to editors and admins only.
indicatorsPage.importAFeedOrAdd: Import a feed, or add one by hand. See Setup.
indicatorsPage.ifItsFeedSendsIt: If its feed sends it again, it comes back. To keep a value from matching, put it on the allow list instead.

feedDialog.theDefaultsFillInWhat: The defaults fill in what an indicator does not say. New defaults apply to what is stored from now on.
feedDialog.name: Name
feedDialog.suchAsOpenctiOrAbuse: Such as OpenCTI or Abuse.ch URLhaus.
feedDialog.manualAddedOneAtA: Manual: added one at a time

importDialog.aFileIndicatorsTheFeed: A {{value}} file. Indicators the feed has are replaced; what cannot be read is listed, never dropped without a word.

feedsPage.whereIndicatorsComeFromA: Where indicators come from. A job sends each feed with the ingest token; an editor can also import a file here.
feedsPage.addTheFirstFeedThen: Add the first feed, then import into it. See Setup.
feedsPage.itsAreDeletedWithIt: Its {{plural}} are deleted with it, and stop matching at once.

allowDialog.everyLookupAnswersAllowedUntil: Every lookup answers allowed until it ends, whatever a feed says. A block allows every address in it.
allowDialog.requiredWhyItIsFine: Required: why it is fine, for whoever reads it next.
allowDialog.forADomainItsSubdomains: For a domain: its subdomains too

allowListPage.valuesKnownToBeFine: Values known to be fine: your own scanners, partners, a shared host a feed blames. Each has a reason and an end.
allowListPage.valuesAFeedGetsWrong: Values a feed gets wrong go here, with a reason and an end date.

setupPage.addAFeedThenSend: Add a feed, then send it from a job as often as its source changes. Other products look values up with the same token.
setupPage.theBodyIsTheFeed: The body is the feed's kind: a STIX 2.1 bundle, a CSV with a value column, or one value per line. Gzip is fine. Use THREAT_INTEL_INGEST_TOKEN, set where threat-intel runs, or an API token with the editor role.
setupPage.whatSiemVpnWafAnd: What SIEM, VPN, WAF and DAST ask. Up to 1000 values in one call.
setupPage.aMatchWithConfidence60: A match with confidence 60 or more is malicious; below that, suspicious. A value nobody has is not known, which is not the same as safe.
setupPage.anAddressAlsoMatchesThe: An address also matches the blocks that hold it; a domain also matches parents added with their subdomains.
setupPage.indicatorsEndOnTheirValid: Indicators end on their valid-until date, or after the feed's default days. STIX patterns an indicator list cannot hold, such as AND, are listed in the import's answer.
setupPage.tlpRedIsForNamed: TLP:RED is for named recipients: viewers never see it, and their lookups answer as if it were not there.

settingsPage.askAnAdminOfThis: Ask an admin of this threat-intel for access.
